bullets.title: NVDA: New China-specific AI chip planned for small-batch year-end shipments; Vera Rubin racks now at OpenAI
bullets.body: NVIDIA is developing a new AI chip compliant with US export controls specifically for Chinese customers, with small-batch shipments targeted by year-end; several Chinese customers have already placed orders though Beijing approval is uncertain. Separately, NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks are now powering OpenAI's training infrastructure, and Hudson River Trading signed a multi-billion compute deal with CoreWeave to access Vera Rubin and HGX B200 GPUs. On the negative side, INTC and NVDA showed the most bearish options flow intraday, and ORCL and NVDA CDS hit all-time wides as post-July risk rally fades.

bullets.title: BMO Capital initiates semi coverage: NVDA at $340 PT (+57%), MU $1300 (+33%), AVGO $455 (+25%)
bullets.body: BMO's Harsh Kumar initiates broad semiconductor coverage with outperform ratings: NVDA $340 PT (57% upside), MU $1300 (33%), AVGO $455 (25%), MRVL $250, AMD $550 (17%), PI $220 (38%), QBTS $35 (86%); MTSI gets market perform at $335. The sweep of bullish initiations across the AI semiconductor complex is one of the most comprehensive on record.

bullets.title: MRVL: Google signs 7-year warrant deal tying XPU revenue milestones; Roth raises PT to $350
bullets.body: Marvell became the first semiconductor company to receive Google warrants—59M shares at $206.58 strike vesting over FY33 in $500M Custom Products revenue tranches covering AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, and near-memory compute. Roth raised PT from $275 to $350 (Buy); MRVL was up 5.8% on the session. JPM's Harlan Sur hosted a small-group call on MRVL and AVGO developments.

bullets.title: AVGO: Seeking $60B+ AI debt deal; JPM AMA on AVGO scheduled Sept 3
bullets.body: Broadcom is pursuing more than $60B in debt financing tied to AI infrastructure expansion, per Bloomberg. BMO initiated outperform at $455 PT (25% upside). JPM's Harlan Sur is hosting an Ask Me Anything on AVGO on September 3 at 10am ET.

bullets.title: MU: $10B Gigaresearch Lab announced; $250B+ total US commitment; HBM post-era preparations noted
bullets.body: Micron announced a new $10B Idaho Gigaresearch Lab to advance memory and compute technology, uniting academia, government, startups, and industry. Separately, CNBC reported Micron is committing $250B+ in US advanced memory manufacturing and R&D creating 90K+ jobs. SK Hynix commentary noted preparation for a 'post-HBM era' with memory disaggregation emerging as a potential disruption to current HBM business models.

bullets.title: BABA: Hedgeye removes long; cloud missed, e-commerce disappointing, FV $132
bullets.body: Hedgeye removed its BABA long after Q2 Cloud Intelligence Group revenue missed estimates (46.1bn RMB ex-T-Head), CMR revenue fell 8% YoY (worst since June 2022), and international commerce declined for first time since 2022 due to Shopee/TikTok share loss in Southeast Asia. Qwen AI model generated $3.4bn RMB but losses exceeded 4x revenues. Hedgeye's fair value is $132. Alibaba separately guided AI-product annualized revenue toward ~$10B next quarter from $7.3B, and expects higher gross margins as in-house chips replace purchased chips.

bullets.title: ADI: Q3 beat drives analyst target upgrades to $450–$460; AI data center run rate >$3B
bullets.body: Analog Devices beat Q3 on revenue (+39.7% YoY, +2.6% vs consensus) and EPS (+3.3%), guided Q4 above consensus, and raised September price increases. AI-exposed revenue run rate exceeded $3B with data center growth >100% YoY. Citi raised target to $460 (26x CY27 EPS) and Needham to $450; 89% of sell-side is Buy with average target $467 implying 25% upside. NTM P/E at 23.9x vs 5-year average 24x.

bullets.title: SPOT: Upsizes buyback program by $1.5B to ~$2.2B total; stock at $533
bullets.body: Spotify increased its share repurchase authorization by $1.5B on top of the $723M remaining from the prior program, bringing total authorization to approximately $2.223B. Stock was at $533.13 at time of announcement.

bullets.title: CHTR: Down 3.1% after completing Cox/LBRDK deal; SPHR initiated OW at $185 by Piper Sandler
bullets.body: Charter Communications fell 3.1% after closing the Cox and Liberty Broadband acquisition. Piper Sandler initiated Sphere Entertainment at overweight with a $185 price target, citing upside from future Sphere venue expansion and margin benefits. APP and TTD were the main advertising weakness contributors in the communications sector.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Data center REITs remain largest overweight for REIT funds; Trump files $1M EQIX purchase
bullets.body: Citi REIT tracker shows Data Center REITs are the largest sector overweight (+34.98% YTD), led by DLR up ~1%. EQIX, IRM, and EXR saw the largest sequential ownership declines since 3/31. Separately, Trump reportedly filed a stock purchase of up to $1M in Equinix after commenting on data center investment.

bullets.title: COHR/AAOI: Optical sector undervalued; both severely capacity-constrained with exceptional demand
bullets.body: One analyst called COHR and AAOI 'severely capacity-constrained' with 'extremely high' demand visibility, arguing the valuation disconnect is excessive. However, another industry contact warned that manufacturing constraints will delay optical attach timeline growth, and that optical content per rack growth may disappoint vs. elevated expectations.

bullets.title: RBLX: Australia flags child safety issues; engagement tracker shows Q3 bookings tracking well above guidance
bullets.body: Australian regulators identified child safety issues on Roblox, requiring platform changes. On fundamentals, Hedgeye's metaverse tracker shows Q3 bookings model at -6% YoY vs. management's -14-18% guidance, with DAU projected -14.7% YoY for Q3. New user acquisition is slowing meaningfully; Russia unban June 10 is showing positive data impact. Mizuho expert call noted RBLX demand 'generally healthy despite hardware headwinds.'

bullets.title: SMCI: Independent probe clears senior management; board approves export compliance improvements
bullets.body: SuperMicro completed an independent probe and found no evidence current senior management was aware of any alleged chip diversion scheme; terminated employees had violated company rules. The board approved new export compliance program improvements, and shares rose ~1.6% premarket.

bullets.title: INTC: Nova Lake-S draws 296W vs. 125W expected TDP; foundry margin risk if limited to IO tiles
bullets.body: Intel's 28-core Nova Lake-S reportedly draws 296W PL1, approximately 2.4x its expected 125W TDP, raising power efficiency concerns. On the foundry side, one analyst noted Intel foundry margins 'would absolutely crater' if limited to IO tiles and periphery; profitability requires wafer-level work, and management is targeting in-house tiles to improve pricing power.

bullets.title: MSFT/META: Meta quietly among Microsoft's largest AI customers; MSFT Azure demand robust
bullets.body: Bloomberg reported Meta has become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers. Mizuho's expert call confirmed MSFT Azure demand is robust though M365 Copilot success is limited. JPM technical analysis flags hyperscaler basket (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, ORCL) stuck below 2026 range highs, raising vulnerability for the broader AI theme.

bullets.title: MRVL/FN: FN Rosenblatt reiterates Buy at $750 PT; NOK now 11% of FN revenue
bullets.body: Rosenblatt reiterated Buy on Fabrinet with a $750 PT (implying ~70% upside from ~$440) following post-earnings weakness. Nokia now represents 11% of FN's total revenue per Rosenblatt's research, an emerging concentration signal worth monitoring.

bullets.title: NWSA: JPM Overweight; F27 Dow Jones EBITDA margin guided to 28%, $700M buyback planned
bullets.body: JPM maintains Overweight on News Corp (NWSA) with Dec-2027 PT of $38; F27 revenue/EBITDA forecast at $9.3B/$1.8B (+12% EBITDA YoY). Dow Jones targeting ~$1B EBITDA by 2030 with WSJ digital price hikes and improved retention. $700M in share buybacks planned for F27 at $175M/quarter pace.

bullets.title: WIX: JPM downgrades to Underweight; Base44 hits $200M ARR but core decelerating
bullets.body: JPMorgan downgraded Wix to Underweight, citing Base44's $200M ARR growth but noting high churn and monthly-skewed contract mix reduce quality. Creative Subscriptions (ex-Base44) decelerating to low-single-digit growth in 2H26 vs. mid-single-digit in 1H26. Management is aggressively reinvesting in marketing with payoff pushed to 2027.

bullets.title: AMD: Roth maintains Buy, raises CY26/27 revenue forecast on stronger AI Helios uptake
bullets.body: Roth reaffirmed Buy on AMD and raised revenue estimates for CY26/27 based on stronger AI Helios program traction with hyperscale customers, noting Helios products are slightly margin-dilutive due to HBM costs but that CPU demand is accretive to gross margins. PT remains $650.

bullets.title: TSLA: Robotaxi completing unsupervised rides in Austin; FSD competitive commentary mixed
bullets.body: All 170 Tesla Robotaxi rides monitored by Robo Report over the past two weeks in Austin were completed unsupervised. FSD competitive commentary on X was mixed, with one user suggesting advanced AI will eventually simplify FSD development but current competitive pressures are eroding capabilities.
